principles.minimize: Account export and retained privacy/deletion audit include only data required for portability, product operation, security, or lifecycle proof.

export.authentication: authenticated account plus recent password reauthentication
export.audit: successful export is not returned unless a minimal PRIVACY_EXPORT_REQUESTED event is durably recorded

deactivate.authentication: authenticated account plus recent password reauthentication and CSRF
deactivate.behavior: preserve profile and workspace data, set canonical account status DISABLED, revoke all current sessions and require governed administrator reactivation before authentication can resume
deactivate.lastCriticalOwner: rejected until another active OWNER or SUPER_OWNER exists
deactivate.audit: successful deactivation durably records ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED in the canonical identity security-event stream

delete.authentication: authenticated account plus recent password reauthentication and CSRF
delete.lastCriticalOwner: rejected until another active OWNER or SUPER_OWNER exists
delete.audit: successful deletion durably records ACCOUNT_DELETED while the live profile is replaced by the sanitized tombstone

stores.deletion: identity profile is replaced by a minimal tombstone; sessions/devices are removed; user workspace is overwritten with an empty canonical workspace; minimal privacy/deletion audit remains bounded in canonical identity security events
stores.retention: deactivation preserves live account payload while disabling authentication; successful deletion removes live personal account payload; bounded privacy audit and tombstone proof remain until an explicit governed retention policy supersedes this contract
stores.export: current-account export reads canonical identity and workspace state before deletion and records a minimal durable export-request audit event

stores.deletion: same canonical SaveIdentityState/SaveUserWorkspace lifecycle as SQLite; no backend-specific privacy fork
stores.retention: deactivation preserves live account payload while disabling authentication; successful deletion removes live personal account payload; bounded privacy audit and tombstone proof remain until an explicit governed retention policy supersedes this contract
stores.export: same application-level export and audit contract as SQLite

stores.deletion: no account-owned personal payload is persistently cached; deactivated/deleted sessions are denied and account endpoints return Cache-Control no-store
stores.retention: shared market-data cache follows market-data freshness/retention policy and is not account-owned

stores.kind: persistence archive, backup and point-in-time recovery
stores.deletion: immutable historical backups are not falsely claimed to be rewritten in place; current-target tombstones are carried forward during replace restore and tombstoned archived workspaces are scrubbed before restore
stores.retention: backup/PITR copies expire under the operator backup-retention policy; a point older than deletion must not be reopened to service without replaying a later authoritative deletion tombstone state
stores.export: backup archives are operator recovery artifacts and are not returned by the self-service account export

stores.kind: bounded canonical identity security/privacy audit plus minimal retained deletion proof
stores.deletion: the deleted UserRecord is sanitized to userId, tenantId, deletion timestamp, controlled reason code and tombstone marker; bounded privacy events retain only event id/type, tenant/user identifiers and timestamp for the implemented self-service privacy lifecycle
stores.retention: bounded security/privacy events provide operational evidence; deletion tombstone remains to prevent silent resurrection and prove deletion until a later governed legal/retention policy explicitly changes it
stores.export: privacy audit is operator evidence and is not injected into the self-service account payload; export itself records a durable request event before data is returned

dataClasses.deactivate: preserved with status DISABLED; authentication is denied until governed reactivation
dataClasses.tombstone: original username, displayName, role, password hash and login history are not retained

dataClasses.export: included as current UI preference state
dataClasses.tombstone: only the non-secret userId remains on the empty workspace row

dataClasses.delete: all personal symbols are removed by the empty-workspace overwrite

dataClasses.export: included as an empty array with categoryStatus=not-persisted-per-user because v19.0.0 has no canonical user-owned persisted research metadata
dataClasses.delete: no user-owned persistent rows exist to delete

dataClasses.export: included as an empty array with categoryStatus=not-persisted-per-user because v19.0.0 has no canonical user-owned feedback store
dataClasses.delete: no user-owned persistent rows exist to delete

dataClasses.export: included as safe device/session identifiers, labels, state and timestamps
dataClasses.deactivate: sessions are revoked; device records remain part of the preserved account security state
dataClasses.delete: all account device and session records are removed
dataClasses.tombstone: device fingerprints, token hashes, MFA proof and other credential material are never retained in the deletion tombstone

dataClasses.deactivate: password/MFA credential state remains server-side only so governed reactivation does not require destructive reset; active sessions are revoked
dataClasses.delete: password hash/MFA credentials disappear with the live user profile; session token hashes and device fingerprint hashes disappear with session/device records

dataClasses.export: not injected into the self-service payload; successful export records PRIVACY_EXPORT_REQUESTED before response
dataClasses.tombstone: bounded canonical audit retains event id/type, tenant/user identifiers and timestamp only for these privacy lifecycle events

dataClasses.export: not part of a pre-deletion self-export
dataClasses.delete: retained intentionally as minimal deletion proof and anti-resurrection state
dataClasses.tombstone: userId, tenantId, deletedAt and controlled reason code only

operatorAccess.normal: operators use existing role/rights boundaries; there is no operator endpoint that exposes password hashes, raw tokens or device fingerprints
operatorAccess.privacyAudit: privacy lifecycle events reuse the existing bounded tenant-scoped privileged identity security-event projection; no parallel privacy audit store or secret-bearing event payload is introduced
operatorAccess.deletedAccount: the sanitized identity tombstone may remain visible to authorized identity operators as deletion proof; no original profile, watchlist, session or device secret is recoverable from live canonical state
operatorAccess.restore: replace restore automatically carries forward tombstones already present on the target; disaster recovery to a fresh target from a point older than deletion requires replay of a later authoritative tombstone state before service is enabled
operatorAccess.legalRetention: provider/legal retention obligations remain separate from product-owned account data; any future legal hold must be explicit, scoped and added to this inventory rather than silently retaining user payload

host016Dependency: Application-level archive anti-resurrection is executable now. Real managed-hosted backup/PITR retention, fresh-target recovery, operator replay and restore-drill proof remains a Development technical dependency on HOST-016 and must not be inferred from this contract alone.
